name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, metallising, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: Results week, and a governance shock. Xpro India's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY: the new Barjora dielectric line has moved to commercial orders, but ultra-thin grades are still in customer validation. Cosmo First's PAT roughly doubled, but its release does not mention capacitor film. Jindal Poly took its co-investor Brookfield to the NCLT over the management of JPFL Films, the subsidiary that houses its capacitor film.
key_points: Xpro India, Q2 FY27 (reported 3 Nov): revenue was Rs 176.7 cr (+47.4% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA from operations Rs 16.4 cr (9.3% margin). The results summary gives PAT as Rs 9.5 cr (S24); Screener shows consolidated net profit of Rs 7.19 cr (S19). Barjora supplies have moved to commercial orders, while ultra-thin and higher-end grades remain under customer validation. Power disruptions slowed the ramp-up (S24).

Xpro's UAE dielectric line: mechanical installation is nearly complete and equipment trials have started, but no start date was given (S24). The board approved an AED 83 mn guarantee to refinance the UAE subsidiary's loan (S19). The stock rose 10.7% on 4 Nov to Rs 1,103, or 73.5x P/E (S19).

Cosmo First, Q2 FY27 (3 Nov): revenue was Rs 1,388 cr versus Rs 919 cr a year earlier, and net profit Rs 99 cr versus Rs 47 cr (S14). Profit was helped by a Rs 24.8 cr customs-duty write-back and a concessional tax-regime benefit. The release does not mention capacitor film or the second metalliser (S23). The stock trades at 9.3x P/E (S14).

Jindal Poly: on 2 Nov it filed an NCLT oppression petition against JPFL Films and Brookfield affiliate Project Holdings Fourteen (DIFC), its co-investor under a Mar 2022 shareholders' agreement. The investor had served a SIAC arbitration notice on 16 Oct (S25). This adds to the open SEBI show-cause notice of 6 Aug (S6). CRISIL put JPFL's operational capacitor capacity at 5,000 TPA (S7); the Rs 250 cr doubling (S4) is still unconfirmed.

SRF commissioned the first phase of its Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant on 15 May 2026, at about Rs 277 cr (S9). On the 22 Oct call, management said sales are ahead of plan at 'a significant premium to vanilla film' (S20), and a second line is 'likely sooner than later' (S22).

Market size (unchanged): QYResearch puts global capacitor-grade BOPP at USD 874.5 mn in 2025, reaching USD 1,336.2 mn by 2032 (6.25% CAGR) (S21). IndexBox forecasts 6-9% annual growth over 2026-35, with EV power electronics at 10-14% (S1).

Week to 4 Nov (Screener, vs 28 Oct): Xpro rose about 10% and Cosmo about 8% on results; Jindal Poly rose about 4% and SRF about 3% (S14, S15, S16, S19). All four remain 20-32% below their 52-week highs.

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Xpro India has the most direct exposure: dielectric film made up Rs 135.52 cr of FY26 sales (S17). Q2 revenue rose 47% YoY as Barjora supplies turned into commercial orders (S24). At 73.5x P/E (S19), the market already prices in a lot of growth.
SRF: capacitor BOPP has been commercial since the May 2026 commissioning, at a premium to standard film (S9, S20). It remains small within trailing group sales of Rs 18,265 cr (S16).
Cosmo First: profit rose on specialty films and chemicals (S23). At 9.3x P/E (S14), the market gives no value to its capacitor line (900 MT/yr metalliser, S3).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Jindal Poly: JPFL Films, where the capacitor business sits, is now caught in an NCLT petition, a SIAC arbitration and court proceedings with its Brookfield co-investor (S15, S25). The SEBI notice is still open (S6), CRISIL has the ratings on Watch Negative (S7), and trailing net loss is Rs 991 cr (S15).

Domestic supply is building fast. SRF is commercial and plans a second line (S9, S22), Xpro is heading to 13,000 MT (S18), JPFL has 5,000 TPA (S7), and ECMS has approved several metallised-film projects (S11, S12). No source we could verify quantifies Indian demand.

Qualification is slow: Xpro's ultra-thin grades, the EV-relevant end of the market, are still being validated by customers (S24). Polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Xpro: UAE line start-up, Barjora ultra-thin grade approvals, and any dielectric volume figures (S24).
Jindal Poly: Q2 FY27 results (not yet filed as of 5 Nov), and the outcome of the NCLT, SIAC and court proceedings over JPFL (S15, S25).
SRF: a board decision on a second capacitor-film line (S22).
Any new ECMS tranche, and Finance Ministry notification of DGTR's PET-film anti-dumping recommendation; the PET case does not cover BOPP (S8, S12).

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film, the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates. It is mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it at 2.5-12 micron, in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, for AC and DC capacitors (S2). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film for power capacitors, EV systems and railways, including ultra-thin, hazy and semi-rough grades (S17). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has no comparable purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer lets the capacitor 'self-heal': a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the part.

Demand is moving to thinner films with higher breakdown voltage. IndexBox sees EV demand shifting to 2-4 micron BOPP. It expects BOPP to keep 60-70% of volume, with metallised film at 40-50% of value (S1). Cosmo's metallised grades show the range of end uses:

items: Al-Zn standard: fans, motor-run and AC capacitors (S3).
Slope/RMF: APFC panels and wind turbines (S3).
Segmented: power supplies and DC-DC converters (S3).
'Series': variable-frequency drives, renewable inverters, UPS and EVs (S3).

blocks.text: Xpro says demand is 'structural, not cyclical', driven by electrification, renewables, grid modernisation and traction (S17). This week Xpro said its ultra-thin and higher-end grades are still under customer validation (S24). That underlines how long qualification takes at the thin end of the range.

blocks.text: The two forecasts agree on mid-to-high single-digit growth. QYResearch names Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group among global suppliers, alongside Toray, Oji, Shin-Etsu, Bolloré, Tervakoski and several Chinese producers (S21). We did not re-verify Mordor and FMI figures, so they are left out. We found no verified figure for the size of the Indian market.

When Cosmo launched capacitor film in Dec 2023, it said the product was largely imported from China, and saw room for import substitution and exports (S2). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). We found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duties of USD 54-366/t on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand (S8). As of 5 Nov we found no Finance Ministry notification. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric (S1). We found no capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action.

subsections.title: Confirmed producers: what changed this week

blocks.text: Xpro India: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47.4% YoY, but only 1.3% QoQ. Barjora's initial supplies have turned into commercial orders, while ultra-thin and higher-end grades remain under customer validation. Recurring external power disruptions slowed the ramp-up (S24). No dielectric volume was disclosed. The board approved an AED 83 mn corporate guarantee to refinance the UAE subsidiary's loan, and appointed Girish Behal MD-CEO from 1 Jan 2027 (S19). The two profit figures differ: the results summary shows PAT of Rs 9.5 cr (S24), while Screener's consolidated line shows Rs 7.19 cr (S19). Both are given here.

Cosmo First: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,388 cr, against Rs 919 cr a year earlier, and net profit Rs 99 cr, against Rs 47 cr (S14). The quarter included a Rs 24.8 cr EBITDA write-back of US-subsidiary customs duty, a Rs 7 cr inventory loss and a concessional tax-regime benefit. Net debt fell to Rs 1,057 cr (1.9x EBITDA). The release covers specialty chemicals, coated films (16k MT expansion in H2 FY27) and Plastech, but does not mention capacitor film (S23). The website still describes the second metalliser as forthcoming (S3).

SRF: phase 1 of the Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant was commissioned on 15 May 2026 at about Rs 277 cr (S9). On the Q2 call, management said the product has key customer approvals and sells at a significant premium to vanilla film (S20), and that a second line is likely (S22). SRF does not disclose capacitor-film revenue.

Jindal Poly Films: Q2 FY27 results had not been filed as of 5 Nov, and the June quarter is the latest on Screener (S15). The petition filed on 2 Nov alleges that Brookfield affiliate Project Holdings Fourteen (DIFC) has engaged in oppression and mismanagement at JPFL Films since Mar 2024. The investor's SIAC arbitration notice of 16 Oct alleges breaches of the Mar 2022 shareholders' agreement. On 30 Oct it sought interim measures in the Delhi High Court. The company says the financial impact is 'unquantifiable at this stage' (S25). Screener's filing list shows the Delhi HC petition was disposed of, and a Singapore court granted an interim anti-suit injunction on 2 Nov (S15).

Only Xpro India has reported capacitor-film volume and revenue separately, in its FY26 annual report (S17). Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly would be an estimate, so none is given.

items: Pan Electronics (India), BSE 517397: a Bengaluru micro-cap that has metallised polypropylene and polyester dielectric films since 1986 and has moved into MPP capacitors (S13). It is a potential base-film buyer, but immaterial in size.
Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and power-factor panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S5). We found no disclosed film-supply tie-up.

Polyplex and UFlex (Flex Films): IndexBox lists both among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1), but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade. The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to Polyplex (S8).

blocks.text: Coverage gap: the main domestic film-capacitor makers (TDK India, Vishay India) and the ECMS metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) are unlisted or not confirmed as listed (S11, S12). The listed exposure is therefore:

items: Small caps: Xpro, Cosmo and Jindal Poly.
A micro-cap metalliser: Pan Electronics.
A large cap where capacitor film is a small business: SRF.

blocks.text: We found no mid-cap pure play.

blocks.text: Both results-week gains followed earnings, not capacitor news. Xpro rose 10.7% on 4 Nov after revenue grew 47% (S19, S24). Cosmo's move followed a profit jump driven by specialty chemicals and one-offs (S14, S23). Only Xpro, the one producer with large, disclosed exposure, trades at a theme-style multiple of 73.5x P/E. Cosmo is at 9.3x (S14, S19). Jindal Poly trades at about 1.0x book despite the new JPFL dispute (S15). We could not confirm 6- and 12-month returns from a source we opened, so they are left out.

Broker and media coverage remains thin. SRF's Q2 write-ups mention capacitor film alongside chemicals and battery foil (S20, S22). Cosmo's and Xpro's results coverage focuses on overall growth (S23, S24). We found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost (S1). Cosmo booked a Rs 7 cr inventory loss on falling raw-material prices in Q2 (S23).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), and India's imports came mostly from China (S2).
Qualification lag: Xpro's ultra-thin grades are still under customer validation, and power disruptions slowed the Barjora ramp-up (S24).
Domestic supply build-out: SRF's line plus a likely second line (S9, S22), Xpro to 13,000 MT (S18), JPFL at 5,000 TPA (S7). We found no verified figure for Indian demand.
Small share of revenue: specialty chemicals, packaging films and one-offs drove Cosmo's Q2 (S23), and capacitor film is small within SRF's sales (S16).
Governance at Jindal Poly: the NCLT, SIAC arbitration and court proceedings over JPFL with its Brookfield co-investor (S25), the open SEBI notice (S6) and CRISIL's Watch Negative (S7).
Start of production at Xpro's UAE line, and customer approval of its ultra-thin Barjora grades (S24).
Jindal Poly's Q2 FY27 results and the course of the JPFL dispute (S15, S25); confirmation of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S4, S7).
An SRF board decision on a second capacitor-film line (S22).
ECMS metallised-film projects (Dhruv, Capfilm) coming on stream, and any new ECMS tranche (S11, S12).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S8). No trade action specific to capacitor BOPP has been found.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric base-film maker at Barjora (2-16 micron). FY26 dielectric sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S17), and India capacity was doubled to 8,000 MT in Mar 2026 (S18). QYResearch names it among global players (S21).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY as Barjora moved to commercial orders. Ultra-thin grades are still in validation, and the UAE line is in trials (S24). At 73.5x P/E after a 10.7% one-day jump (S19), execution has to keep pace.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned phase 1 of its Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant on 15 May 2026 at about Rs 277 cr (S9). Holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S10).
companies.impact: Sales are ahead of plan at a premium to standard film, and a second line is likely (S20, S22). Small within Rs 18,265 cr of group sales (S16), but SRF is the fastest-scaling domestic competitor.

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP, launched in Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2). The metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second forthcoming (S3).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 PAT roughly doubled to Rs 99 cr (S14), but capacitor film went unmentioned; earnings are driven by specialty chemicals and films (S23). Trades at 9.3x P/E (S14).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S7), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S4). QYResearch lists the B.C. Jindal group among global players (S21).
companies.impact: A new NCLT and arbitration dispute with Brookfield's affiliate over JPFL (S25) adds to the SEBI notice (S6) and a Rs 991 cr trailing loss (S15). Governance now outweighs the capacitor theme.

companies.name: Pan Electronics (India) Ltd
companies.role: Bengaluru micro-cap that metallises polypropylene and polyester dielectric films (since 1986) and now makes MPP capacitors (S13).
companies.impact: A potential buyer of domestic base film, but immaterial in investment terms given its tiny size (S13).

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S5).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows. No film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S5).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that IndexBox lists among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade. The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to it (S8).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP/BOPET films; IndexBox lists it among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S1).

method:
Weekly refresh of the 2026-W44 edition, researched on 5 Nov 2026 with web search and page fetches. New this week:
- Q2 FY27 results from Xpro India, from the results summary (S24) and Screener (S19). Those two sources give different profit figures, and both are shown.
- Q2 FY27 results from Cosmo First, from the company press release (S23) and Screener (S14).
- Jindal Poly's 2 Nov NCLT petition against Brookfield's affiliate over JPFL Films (S25), and the related court filings listed on Screener (S15).
- SRF's 15 May 2026 commissioning of its Indore capacitor BOPP plant, cited from a ScanX article seen in search results (S9). The page itself returned HTTP 403 when fetched.

Searches found:
- No Jindal Poly Q2 FY27 results yet.
- No new ECMS tranche.
- No Finance Ministry notification of PET-film anti-dumping duty.
- No SRF board approval for a second capacitor line.
- No confirmation of JPFL's doubling.

Carried over without re-opening this week: IndexBox, QYResearch, the Cosmo capacitor web page, CRISIL and the ECMS sources.

Prices: Screener closes for 4 Nov, fetched 5 Nov, for Xpro, Cosmo and Jindal Poly; SRF is from the supplied 4 Nov Screener dataset. Weekly changes are measured against the 28 Oct prices in the W44 edition.

Dropped to keep to 25 sources: the ICICI Direct SRF note, the IIFL Pan Electronics profile, the UFlex product page and the Cosmo Q1 deck. Source IDs were renumbered.

We could not open the 2023 Cosmo call transcript (timeout), so its India market-size figure is not used.

Not stated because not confirmed: capacitor-film revenue for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly, Indian import tonnage or market size, and 6- and 12-month returns.

No ratings or price targets are given.
